observations_and_questions.classification: conditional current source candidate for central alias reconciliation, not an accepted unique count
observations_and_questions.trace: Host longest_guide takes the maximum of Haircut top/front/sides/back, separately includes the fringe and dome, applies variation, and derives max_path with a 301-point floor and two extra slots. It does not include clipper or a bound for overshoot of around’s cosine interpolation. The packed shader receives clipper and all four base lengths; its cut_length uses clipper in the clip/strip branches and uses the same cosine series. It caps requested steps to max_path minus one before writing the path and resamples the result.
conditional_examples: If an otherwise accepted haircut has top/front/sides/back=0.1m, clipper=0.8m, clip=0.5, fade=0, no fringe/hemline/dome, zero variation, and a sampled root with elevation at or below 0.49, the clipped length is 0.8m. The host chooses its 303-point floor, whereas a 0.002m step needs about 400 steps and the shader caps at 302.

Independently, for finite front=0.8m, side=0.8m, back=0.4m, top=0.8m, no clip/strip/fringe/hemline/dome and zero variation, the ideal cosine series at cos(azimuth)=0.5 is 0.85m. A root with elevation in [0,0.25] gets that ring value because smoothstep contributes zero, despite longest() reporting 0.8m. A gap of roughly 0.05m remains well beyond binary32 rounding at this scale; if that root and prior operations occur, requested 0.002m steps exceed the host estimate.
observations_and_questions.limits: These are mathematical source arguments, not constructed hair, sampling, GPU allocation, native shader parsing, dispatch, rendered output or measurement. Supported custom haircut values, corresponding sampled roots, floating/native behavior, previous-stage success and effect on generated hair are unproved. A cap is present, so this trace does not assert an out-of-bounds path write. Original rig F067 and REVIEW-HAIR-GUIDE-MAX-PATH-95E cover extreme raw length/host integer overflow; the above underestimation is a different source condition within related capacity ownership, with exact global alias and remedy unresolved.
observations_and_questions.future_direction: Establish the actual admitted haircut domain and a conservative maximum of all active cut branches and angular interpolation (or a safe variable-length/overflow policy); align host capacity, shader stopping and CPU behavior while preserving intentional clipping, fringe and dome semantics. Later acceptance requires separately authorized product validation.

observations_and_questions.classification: ordinary admitted factor / source policy and documented semantics question; no count or visual result asserted
observations_and_questions.trace: HairShape states every cut length is scaled, accepts a finite factor such as 0.5 and applies Haircut::scaled. That function multiplies top/front/sides/back and adjusts hemline/dome, but leaves clipper and fringe.drop unchanged. Under the selected BowlCut and a root satisfying Fringe::holds, the subsequent declared strand length is 0.1 + 0.048 = 0.148m before and after that scale, and its cut line uses the unchanged drop; Undercut clipper likewise stays 0.008m while the four ordinary lengths are halved. Look::random also calls scaled with 0.75–1.25.
observations_and_questions.limits: Whether a length control should preserve an eyebrow-aligned fringe and close-cropped clipper setting, or scale those cut features, is a design question. A matching sampled root, actual generation or visual change was not shown. Existing F067 and q381 concern distinct extreme-length and one-point-resampling first cuts; global aliases require reconciliation.

nonfindings: The clipped branch is not evidence that a cut enum must be immutable: Cut describes its starting preset while mutable details are intentional.
Fringe and dome are explicitly included in host longest_guide, so the maximum-length question must not claim they are simply ignored.
The selected studio uses a finite positive fixed 0.004m scalp cell, narrowing but not closing public grid admission concerns.
The GPU path has an explicit step cap; no unchecked path write is concluded from an underestimated length.
CPU and GPU same-group parting and their fallback conditions remain separate from haircut-length capacity and are not merged here.

thirteen_lenses.producer-propagation: Finite creator shape and random look call scaled; haircut fields feed CPU comb and packed shader/host capacity. All external custom producers and native outputs remain open.
thirteen_lenses.existing-type-owners: Cut is original preset identity; Haircut, Fringe and Head carry distinct length, morphology and frame semantics. Existing owners should govern capacity and scaling, not a generic numeric wrapper.
thirteen_lenses.admission-contracts: Mannequin geometry is finite and nondegenerate; public mutable Head, Haircut, Serde, scaled factor and mesh cell admit broader values. Existing extreme input questions remain separate.
thirteen_lenses.invariant-operations: Scaling mutates ordinary lengths but not clipper/fringe; longest may underbound active length. Grid extent/add/multiply and normalization require their own supported input contract.
thirteen_lenses.aggregate-states: Head radius and capsule endpoint relationships, haircut length fields and shader capacity must remain coherent through construction, mutation and packing.
thirteen_lenses.wrong-duplicate-owners: CPU and shader duplicate around/cut_length; host owns capacity. Shared equations do not prove a single correct owner without matching executable contracts.
thirteen_lenses.redundant-authority: Stored preset Cut describes origin while mutable controls determine actual hair; that is intentional provenance, unlike independently computed maximum estimates that can underbound active branches.
thirteen_lenses.behavior-preservation: Preserve deliberate fringe, fade, strip, clipper, dome and hemline design choices and selected 0.004m grid while deciding the scale and capacity policy.
thirteen_lenses.enum-state-shape: Cut is a closed preset enum, while hemline/fringe optional and zero fade/strip/dome are intentional independent controls; no blanket enum conversion is inferred.
thirteen_lenses.derivability: Cut/Fringe/Haircut derive Serde/value traits; validate actual persisted policy and checked conversions rather than replacing derives mechanically.
thirteen_lenses.granularity: Lengths, signed heights, normalized elevation, angles and growth factors have different units/ranges; zero and negative values must be considered per feature.
thirteen_lenses.raw-strings: Preset names are display labels and native shader names are boundary identifiers. No closed user-authored string namespace or automatic string defect was established.
thirteen_lenses.raw-primitives: Head geometry, resolution cell, finite normals, hairline position, smoothing thresholds and hair length need dimensional and bounded-resource contracts; do not impose one universal limit.
